findings.summary: All three RuleListTest cases are green only because the author's index currently stages buildSrc/*, which triggers the shared-build escalation to all eight modules. The gate is invoked with no args and no GATE_SCOPE, so its scope is `git diff --cached`. With an empty index it exits at `ok no module changed` BEFORE the CHECK_MODULE_PRINT_RULES door (line 271 precedes line 289), so value() finds no NO_HTTP line and theGateAppliesBothRulesToTheRealTree sees no count line. Verified against a clean clone of this exact tree with the staged scripts and tests copied in: `./gradlew -p buildSrc test` -> 61 tests completed, 3 failed (RuleListTest 3/3, at :45, :77, :45). Re-staging everything in that clone turns it green again. The suite's outcome is a function of the git index, not of the code under test, so this commit does not leave the tree green for anyone who runs the harness suite without a staged shared-build path -- including immediately after the commit lands.
findings.surviving_mutation: Not a surviving mutation -- the dual defect: the test fails while production is correct. Reproduce: clone the repo, copy the staged scripts/check-module.sh, scripts/lib.sh, buildSrc/build.gradle.kts and buildSrc/src/test into it, run ./gradlew -p buildSrc test with an empty index. 3 failures, production untouched. Conversely, any staged scope that is not shared-build also reddens it: staging only format/ gives 'rule5 applied to 1' against an expectation of 4.

findings.summary: The WT26 residual is closed for rule 5 only by the index-dependent test in WT29. Every hermetic scenario has the NO_HTTP branch running either 0 times (fullScope..., alpha/beta) or exactly 1 time (theRuleCounterCountsRatherThanRestates, alpha/format). A constant assignment inside the branch satisfies both. Verified: `applied_r5=$((applied_r5+1))` -> `applied_r5=1` leaves all 12 ModuleGateTest cases green; the only red is RuleListTest.theGateAppliesBothRulesToTheRealTree. So the counter-versus-restatement property rests entirely on the one test that is broken in a clean checkout -- fix WT29 by narrowing or dropping that assertion and the restatement mutation returns silently.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:332 `applied_r5=$((applied_r5+1))` -> `applied_r5=1`. Green across binjava.ModuleGateTest (12/12). Fix: give theRuleCounterCountsRatherThanRestates (or a second scenario) a fixture with TWO NO_HTTP modules, e.g. include("alpha","format","ingest") expecting `rule5 applied to 2` -- no constant then satisfies 0, 1 and 2.

findings.summary: The one-rule-named-module fixture was built for NO_HTTP and never for NO_CLOUD. Every test expects `rule2 to 0` (both scratch scenarios: alpha/beta and alpha/format name no NO_CLOUD module) or `rule2 to 2` (RuleListTest, real tree). A constant 2 satisfies the real tree and never executes in the scratch runs, so it satisfies the zeros too. Verified against the FULL suite, not a subset: 61 tests, BUILD SUCCESSFUL. `applied_r2` is therefore still a restatement, which is exactly the property this round set out to remove; the fix landed on one of the two rules.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:364 `applied_r2=$((applied_r2+1))` -> `applied_r2=2`. Green across ALL 61 tests. Fix: add `client` (or `plugin`) to the theRuleCounterCountsRatherThanRestates fixture's settings and assert `rule5 applied to 1, rule2 to 1`.

findings.summary: Answer to the round-8 question: yes, there is a third way, and it is one the counts cannot see by construction. The counters prove the BRANCH was entered, never that the right predicate ran inside it. Swapping the two group variables between the two rule blocks -- grep CLOUD_GROUPS inside the NO_HTTP branch and HTTP_GROUPS inside the NO_CLOUD branch -- leaves both counts reading exactly `rule5 applied to 4, rule2 to 2` while both rules are inert (format/ingest are checked for cloud SDKs, client/plugin for HTTP). Verified: all 61 tests green. This is the M0.23 class and the backlog row is correct to defer it, but the row names only 'emptying HTTP_GROUPS, dropping compileClasspath, disabling the rule-4 check'; the swap deserves a mention because it is the member that specifically defeats the anti-shadow counters added this round. Separately: rule 4 and the plugin/binstore-backends half of rule 2 have no counter at all, so the summary line 'rule2 applied to N' names one of the two rule-2 checks.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:333 HTTP_GROUPS -> CLOUD_GROUPS and :365 CLOUD_GROUPS -> HTTP_GROUPS. 61/61 green, summary line byte-identical.

findings.summary: anEmptyDependencyReportIsNotCompliance asserts only exit 1 and the absence of 'module(s) checked'. Its sibling aModuleThatFailsToBuildFailsTheGate does assert the reason ('build failed'); this one does not, so it cannot distinguish 'the empty report was rejected before the rules ran' from 'the gate failed for some other reason and the success line was suppressed'. Verified surviving mutation below leaves the gate exiting 1 while falling through to `checked=$((checked+1))` and applying rules 5 and 2 to an EMPTY deps string -- i.e. the rules silently pass over nothing for every module, which is the precise failure the test's own javadoc says it exists to prevent.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:320 `[ -n "$one" ] || { bad_conf="$conf (empty report)"; break; }` -> `[ -n "$one" ] || { fail "$m: empty report"; break; }`. bad_conf stays empty, the `continue` is skipped, the module is counted as checked and both rules grep an empty report. ModuleGateTest 12/12 green. Fix: add `.contains("could not resolve")`.

findings.summary: Tier. theGateAppliesBothRulesToTheRealTree runs the unstubbed gate against the real tree, which under the shared-build escalation spawns 8 real `./gradlew :m:build` plus 16 `:m:dependencies` invocations from inside the buildSrc test JVM -- a nested Gradle build in what build.md calls the L0 layer. Measured in a clean clone: 14 s with a staged shared-build path, 2 s without. The .harness/check-module-*.log files for all eight modules, timestamped 04:22, are the harness suite's own footprint. build.md as edited by this commit says the cold-daemon case is unmeasured; that unmeasured cost is now inside the harness suite that check-harness-tests.sh runs on every scripts/*.sh commit. Closing WT29 with a hermetic scratch fixture (WT30/WT31) removes this too, which is why it is worth doing that way rather than by pinning GATE_SCOPE=full.

Answer to the round-8 redundancy question. ModulePlanTest.planNamesTheModulesItWillBuild dominates ModuleSelectionTest on every row except `format/A.java format/B.java nope/C.java | 1` (sort -u dedupe plus an unknown top-level directory): both drive the same selection, but --plan drives it through the production composition while --select-modules is a test-only door of the kind the script's own header blames for the 'helpers tested, production untouched' round. Folding that one row into ModulePlanTest would let the --select-modules flag be deleted. Not blocking, and not a request to delete a test (non-negotiable 2) -- recorded as the honest answer that ~10 of the 61 constrain nothing ModulePlanTest does not. The rest of the suite is not redundant: ModuleDriftTest's `clean`/four-character-`http` case, ModuleListDerivationTest's three line shapes, and the twelve ModuleGateTest production-door scenarios each kill a mutation no sibling kills.

Answer to the round-8 question about deleting `beta`: no, the scenario was not weakened. The discrimination comes from `format` being the only NO_HTTP member among the selected modules, and keeping beta would have given `3 module(s) checked, rule5 applied to 1` -- identical discriminating power. Deleting it was forced by fixture consistency (beta leaves settings, so its tracked build file becomes a legitimate orphan and the drift halt would mask the assertion), and the test still asserts a positive count rather than an absence. Recorded for the record, no action. Similarly on the stub-rewrite question: the two variants' `case "$1" in *:build)` / `*:dependencies)` patterns match the gate's real argv (`:alpha:build`, `:alpha:dependencies` are always $1), and any change to how the gate invokes gradlew -- inserting a flag before the task name, renaming the log file -- makes them fail LOUDLY (exit 0 against an expected 1), not pass vacuously. The triplicated stub body across scratch() and the two variants is a maintenance seam, not a disarm path.
